label: Cycle 1 REVEAL
takeaway: The number should feel wrong against what was just shown.
mustBeTrue: One number. It is a year-of-career ordinal, not a calendar year or a quantity of anything.
wouldBeALie: Decoration. Any chart, any second value, anything that invites comparison.

label: Cycle 2 PROVOKE
quote: Latto's biggest is half of everything she's ever streamed. Jay Rock's is fifty-two percent. Ab-Soul's, seventy-one. Biz Markie, seventy-nine.
takeaway: Concentration is the normal, healthy shape. These four are instances of a rule, not a leaderboard.
mustBeTrue: Each percentage is that artist's own biggest song against that artist's own total. Four different denominators.
wouldBeALie: Ranking the four against each other, or putting them on one shared axis. Fifty-two and seventy-nine are not competing numbers.

label: Cycle 4 REVEAL
quote: A hundred and eighty-one. Future has done two hundred thirty-two. Young Thug, three hundred and two. Fewer verses than either, and more streams than anyone: forty-three billion, roughly two hundred forty million a verse.
entityKind: artists with a verse count, plus one derived rate
takeaway: The ground shifts rather than the claim collapsing. He does do a lot of features. That was never the interesting part.
mustBeTrue: Verse counts and stream rates are different quantities and must not share a scale. The per-verse rate is the load-bearing figure.
wouldBeALie: Presenting the lower verse count as the refutation. It is context, not the answer.

label: Cycle 6 REVEAL
quote: Number one as a lead single. Eleven times. As an album. Nine. As somebody else's guest. Four. As a mixtape. Three. As a joint album. Two. As a compilation. One. Thirty releases at number one.
entityKind: release-type categories with independent counts, summing to a total
takeaway: Breadth of format. The list should accumulate rather than arrive whole.
mustBeTrue: Thirty is the sum of six release types. The six are categories of release, not chart positions and not a sequence in time.
wouldBeALie: Ordering the six as a ranking or a timeline. They are independent counts that happen to descend.
